questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A different culture than the scandinavien one. A place with a nice city. Interesting courses. A place with a good study environment

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not the easiest. Hard to get an overview of the university's website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The assistance I got was from the mails we received.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Hard. We looked through many websites and facebook sites and we contacted many people - some were scammers. Look at Airbnb; sometimes they have something relatively cheap if you are more than 2 people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a good idea if you don't want to live in dorms and if you want live another place than were you go to school, so you experience more of the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was too hard to find a place to live if you didn't want to live at the dorms. And it could easily be expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You should be prepared to register at more courses than the ones you found beforehand. Some courses were not available when we had to register and some didn't have enough places. It was a bit stressful, but if you are prepared then it is easier. However, you had a long time to decide on your final courses, so if you regretted one then you had a month or even more to find a new course

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to the teachers, and you could show up at classes to talk to the teachers. They could then help you to get registered or tell you how likely it was for you to get on the course.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: One course was not available and one course i changed two times during the process.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to find other courses than the ones you wanted and have them ready before the registration. And don't panic if you are in queue in many of the courses. Either you will get it or there are many other good opportunities

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The MA-course was hard, but the exam form was easy (Data Science with R). The BA level was a bit mixed, but generally easier than UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You don't get exercises that you sit with for youself or in groups. Only one of my courses had exercises but they were done together with the whole class. Less physical lectures but less breaks during the lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Data Science with R I
International Trade
Institutional economics
Principles of economics
Contemporary crisis and social-ecological transformation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Data Science with R I: no physical attendance, good website to learn, easy exam
Contemporary crisis and social-ecological transformation: very interesting, engaged teacher, the exam was a report and a presentation. A bit chaotic, but was also newly taught

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport very cheap. Restaurants cheap. Beer, wine and drinks very cheap. Sportcenter similar to Denmark. Supermarkets cheaper or similar to Denmark. Housing similar to Copenhagen. Entertainment cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Hard to find a team sport to go to, so I had to find a sportcenter were i could swim and train. No friday bars or anything like that. But the city definitely had opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of trips social events. You could choose a sport course but besides that, impossible to find a team sport to go to.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ESN trips/social events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking. Explore the city. Bars and clubs. Letna park in the summer

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fine, but not many people in Prague speaks good english

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the ESN events or Erasmus in Prague. Talk to the person sitting next to you in class. But there were not many local students, mainly exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier. The service was not good (except for restaurants)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Idk, it was overall fine

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
TRY to find other friends than the ones from your home country
Its temporary, if you feel sad everything will be okay. 
It goes by way faster than you think, so dont postpone things. Just do it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet people from other countries and get more out of my comfort zone. Experience another city and live in another city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To not only be friends with the danish people and to get friends from other countries.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
